title: Lions vs. Bears on Thanksgiving? It Started in 1934
description:
The Lions hosted the Bears on Thanksgiving this week. Their very first Thanksgiving game, in 1934, was against the Bears too: a radio station owner's gamble to fill the stands for a brand-new team.

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:04 The first one: 1934

0:15 They become the Detroit Lions

0:55 A rematch 92 years in the making

A note on the story: George A. Richards, owner of Detroit radio station WJR, bought the NFL's Portsmouth (Ohio) Spartans in 1934 and moved them to Detroit as the Lions. He scheduled the undefeated, defending-champion Bears for Thanksgiving Day and arranged a national broadcast on NBC's 94-station network. The 26,000 seats at University of Detroit Stadium sold out two weeks before the game; the Bears won 19-16. The Lions have played on Thanksgiving every year since, except 1939 to 1944. Thanksgiving football itself is older: college teams played on the holiday from the 1870s, and NFL teams from the league's first season in 1920.

Images: "Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears, Thanksgiving Day 1934" (photographer not identified; Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Detroit Lions team photo, 1934 (Wikipedia, public domain in the US). Dutch Clark (Pueblo Chieftain photo; Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
Sources: Pro Football Hall of Fame, "Thanksgiving Game Tradition Dates to 1934" and "Thanksgiving and the NFL"; History.com (Chris Mueller) on the Lions-Bears Thanksgiving tradition; Detroit Historical Society, "The First Thanksgiving Day Football Game in Detroit".
